newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf "virtually ended" asset sale plan.
newsitem.headline: Elf "virtually ended" asset sale plan.

text.p: French oil group Elf Aquitaine has "virtually ended" its asset sales programme in 1996, chief financial officer Bruno Weymuller.

"We have sold 6.1 billion (francs) in financial assets which leaves us at the end of 1996 with a very limited remainder," he told a news briefing, adding the net result of capital gains and losses in 1996 was less than 100 million francs.
This was due to the sale at lower-than-acquired prices of a stakes such as shares in carmaker Renault.
"We still have 3.5 billion francs in financial participations which are essentially our remaining stake in Renault, in BNP in petrochemical engineering and in Banco Central," he said.

"We believe that we have fulfilled our engagement to put order in our portfolio. The 3.5 billion will change but we have not committed ourselves to further sales nor is there a message that they are untouchable," he said.
